d.d: A pug dog, a small dog of an ancient breed originating in China, having a snub nose, wrinkled face, squarish body, short smooth hair, and curled tail.
A pug moth, often with a descriptive word: any geometrid moth of the tribe Eupitheciini, especially the genus Eupithecia; a geometer moth.
In full pug hood: a hood, sometimes with a short cloak attached, worn by women around the middle of the 18th century.

To fill or stop up (a space) with pug (noun etymology 5, noun sense 1), clay, sawdust, or other material by tamping; (specifically) to fill in (the space between joists of a floor, a partition, etc.) with some material to deaden sound, make fireproof, etc.
To mix and work (wet clay) until flexible, soft, and free from air pockets and suitable for making bricks, pottery, etc.
d.x: to pug clay ready for shaping

d.d: One who fights with their fists, feet, or both, especially a boxer and especially a professional prizefighter.
One who engages in rhetorical attacks, for himself or on behalf of another.
Having a tendency to argue or fight; aggressive, combative.
